    Statistics (computed from the raster pixels)

    Statistics ignore NaN. Standard deviation is the population value. “Compatible pixels” are valid in both acquisitions. Values are linear covariance, unitless; they are not dB unless a dB column says so.

    How to read this data

    • What the layer is. HHHH is a geocoded polarimetric covariance term (the HH channel with itself), stored as a unitless linear number. EcoRadar does not treat it as ordinary backscatter intensity and does not convert it to a physical quantity. The dB option is a log transform for display.
    • What a difference means. A − B only says the stored values differ at a pixel. It does not by itself show glacier movement, ice loss or environmental damage. Acquisition geometry, radiometric calibration, noise floor, speckle, snow and ice surface conditions, and processing choices can all produce differences.
    • Speckle. Single pixels are noisy. These rasters show strong speckle and no filtering is applied, so pixel-to-pixel differences are expected even when nothing changed.
    • Compatible pixels. The difference uses only pixels that are valid (not NaN) in both acquisitions. Pixels valid in one acquisition only are drawn in a separate colour and excluded from the statistics.
    • Georeferencing. Positions come from the GeoTIFF tags (EPSG:3413, 20 m). Longitude and latitude are computed from them with the WGS 84 polar stereographic equations. Image up is the +Y direction of the grid; the arrow in the view shows true north.
    • Scope. This is a demonstration of reading and comparing two observations. It makes no claim about what is happening on the ground.

    Reset workspace?

    This restores the default region, frequency, polarization, date, map layer and playback speed, and clears the acquisition log. Files you already saved are not affected.
    Overview, Data explorer, Compare scenes and Reports use synthetic measurements generated in your browser for education; epochs before the 30 July 2025 launch are a simulated archive. The Real NISAR data view uses two genuine NASA-ISRO NISAR L2 GCOV rasters (HHHH, Greenland), embedded unchanged.
